2607.11270.title: Towards Predictive, Aligned, and Scalable Robot Learning
2607.11270.paper_summary: Learning, at its core, extends beyond memorization to the ability to reason and solve novel problems by navigating a space of possibilities. We introduce Lumo-2, a latent world-action model that generates actions by reasoning over world dynamics in latent space. The learned latent world dynamics capture physically grounded visual transitions, naturally encoding future possibilities and providing a unified substrate for cross-modal alignment. This formulation enables predictive reasoning akin to world modelling while remaining lightweight and focused on physical dynamics relevant to control. Central to our approach is the hypothesis that action generation quality is governed by the geometry of the latent space. We observe that standard reconstruction-based action tokenization objectives induce representations biased toward low-level signal fidelity, leading to misalignment between reconstruction quality and downstream control performance. To address this limitation, we propose a multi-stage modality pre-alignment strategy in which action representations are progressively aligned with latent world dynamics, vision, and language. This process enforces cross-modal consistency, promotes abstraction, and induces a structured latent space for predictive reasoning. We provide a systematic empirical study of latent world modelling and modality alignment, analyzing their roles in scaling laws and out-of-distribution generalization. Results show that Lumo-2 consistently outperforms strong vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action model (WAM) baselines, with gains on challenging real-world tasks requiring temporal reasoning, physical understanding, or high control complexity, including long-horizon and dexterous manipulation. These findings suggest that structured multimodal alignment and predictive reasoning are fundamental principles for advancing embodied intelligence.
2607.11270.paper_summary_zh: 學習的核心超越了單純的記憶，轉向通過在可能性空間中導航來推理和解決新問題的能力。<lb/>我們介紹了 Lumo-2，一種潛在世界行動模型，通過在潛在空間中推理世界動態來生成行動。<lb/>學習到的潛在世界動態捕捉了物理基礎的視覺過渡，自然編碼未來的可能性，並為跨模態對齊提供了統一的基礎。<lb/>這一公式使得預測性推理類似於世界建模，同時保持輕量級，專注於與控制相關的物理動態。<lb/>我們方法的核心假設是，行動生成的質量受潛在空間幾何的影響。<lb/>我們觀察到，標準的基於重建的行動標記目標會引起偏向低級信號保真度的表示，導致重建質量與下游控制性能之間的錯位。<lb/>為了解決這一限制，我們提出了一種多階段模態預對齊策略，其中行動表示逐步與潛在世界動態、視覺和語言對齊。<lb/>這一過程強化了跨模態的一致性，促進了抽象，並為預測性推理引入了一個結構化的潛在空間。<lb/>我們提供了一個系統的實證研究，探討潛在世界建模和模態對齊在規模法則和分佈外泛化中的作用。<lb/>結果顯示，Lumo-2 在強大的視覺-語言-行動 (VLA) 和世界-行動模型 (WAM) 基準上持續表現優越，在需要時間推理、物理理解或高控制複雜度的挑戰性現實任務中獲得了增益，包括長期和靈巧操作。<lb/>這些發現表明，結構化的多模態對齊和預測性推理是推進具身智能的基本原則。
